question.knowledge_point: Evaluating Infinite Limits Using the Laws of Exponents and the Algebra of Limits
question.worked_solution:
We can use the laws of exponents and the algebra of limits to rewrite the given limit, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -\infty }{2}^{3x-8} & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }{2}^{3x}\cdot {2}^{-8} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }{({2}^{3})}^{x}\cdot {2}^{-8} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }{8}^{x}\cdot (\frac{1}{256}) \\  & =(\frac{1}{256})\cdot {lim}_{x\to -\infty }{8}^{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we recall the graph of $y={8}^{x}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13943873/assets/85319605a7c7b57d4c7ed29b8d409e3169f3331775580b91b70e2be99fef7986.png)

From the graph, we see that the function decreases to zero as $x$ decreases. Therefore,

$$
{lim}_{x\to -\infty }{8}^{x}=0.
$$

So, we conclude that 

$$
(\frac{1}{256})\cdot {lim}_{x\to -\infty }{8}^{x}=(\frac{1}{256})\cdot 0=0
$$
